turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Come in please. I will take the blood pressure and pulse before you see the doctor.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes sister.
[SEG0003] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I am her sister. Is it okay if I sit with her?
[SEG0004] person_1 (NURSE): Yes, sit. Reading is blood pressure one hundred eighteen over seventy-six, pulse ninety-two, oxygen saturation ninety-eight percent, temperature thirty-six point eight.
[SEG0005] person_1 (NURSE): Doctor is free. Please go in.
[SEG0006] person_4 (DOCTOR): Right. What is the main trouble?
[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): I am very tired, doctor, and I get breathless, and the periods are very heavy.
[SEG0008] person_4 (DOCTOR): Tired since when?
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): Six months... well, actually one year. I don't know, doctor. It came along with the heavy periods.
[SEG0010] person_4 (DOCTOR): Breathless even sitting?
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): No, only on walking or climbing stairs. Sitting I am alright.
[SEG0012] person_4 (DOCTOR): Chest pain, yes or no?
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): Mm, I suppose sometimes. Not really. I don't know, doctor.
[SEG0014] person_4 (DOCTOR): Heavy periods for how long?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): For one year.
[SEG0016] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Yes, about one year, she has been saying the same at home.
[SEG0017] person_4 (DOCTOR): Pad count?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't know the number, doctor. A packet gets finished in two days. There are clots, big ones. I cannot count them.
[SEG0019] person_4 (DOCTOR): Soaking through at night?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes. The sheet is stained and I change three times or four times. Something like that.
[SEG0021] person_4 (DOCTOR): Period pain?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): Only little cramps. Not bad.
[SEG0023] person_4 (DOCTOR): Hair loss, yes or no?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, a lot of hair falls. Since when, I don't know, doctor. A few months, maybe three, maybe five. I never wrote it down.
[SEG0025] person_4 (DOCTOR): Fever?
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0027] person_4 (DOCTOR): Cough?
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): No cough.
[SEG0029] person_4 (DOCTOR): Weight down?
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't know. Maybe the clothes are loose, I suppose. I didn't check on a scale.
[SEG0031] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Also, doctor, thyroid is there in the family. Mother takes thyroid medicine for years. I take thyroxine fifty micrograms myself for thyroid.
[SEG0032] person_4 (DOCTOR): You had TSH done ever?
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): No, never. I don't know of any test.
[SEG0034] person_4 (DOCTOR): Current medicines?
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): Iron, sometimes only.
[SEG0036] person_4 (DOCTOR): Dose?
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): Ferrous sulphate, hundred milligrams... no, two hundred milligrams. Sorry. I saw the packet. I don't take it daily.
[SEG0038] person_4 (DOCTOR): So not every day?
[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): Sometimes, not really. Many days I skip. I cannot tell you the count.
[SEG0040] person_4 (DOCTOR): Any medicine tried for the bleeding?
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): Tranexamic acid. I took it and then stopped after two days. Acidity was too much.
[SEG0042] person_4 (DOCTOR): Stopped when?
[SEG0043] person_2 (PATIENT): Last year itself. I have not touched it after those two days.
[SEG0044] person_4 (DOCTOR): Folic acid?
[SEG0045] person_2 (PATIENT): It was written on the same slip but I never took it. Not even once.
[SEG0046] person_4 (DOCTOR): Allergies?
[SEG0047] person_2 (PATIENT): No allergies, doctor.
[SEG0048] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): There was a rash in childhood with some cough syrup, I think, but I may be mixing it up.
[SEG0049] person_4 (DOCTOR): Do you remember a rash from syrup?
[SEG0050] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't know, doctor. I don't think I am allergic to anything.
[SEG0051] person_4 (DOCTOR): I am examining now. Conjunctiva is pale. Palms are pale.
[SEG0052] person_4 (DOCTOR): Thyroid is not enlarged to feel. Neck nodes absent.
[SEG0053] person_4 (DOCTOR): No ankle swelling. Lungs clear. Pulse is fast, in keeping with ninety-two.

[SEG0054] person_4 (DOCTOR): Putting it together, this may be iron deficiency from the menstrual loss, it may be a thyroid problem given the family story plus tiredness and hair fall, or it may be a fibroid or other uterine cause. I will not pin it to one thing yet. Let us see what the tests say.
[SEG0055] person_2 (PATIENT): I was scared it is something big. My aunt had a surgery, unrelated, sorry.
[SEG0056] person_4 (DOCTOR): We will do bloods today: full blood count, ferritin, and TSH.
[SEG0057] person_4 (DOCTOR): Pelvic ultrasound we might do later if this bleeding continues like this or the haemoglobin comes very low. Not arranging the scan now.
[SEG0058] person_2 (PATIENT): And the iron tablet?
[SEG0059] person_4 (DOCTOR): Keep the ferrous sulphate at two hundred milligrams and take it every day, after food, not just sometimes.
[SEG0060] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): The taste makes her skip, she told me last week.
[SEG0061] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, it tastes like metal, so I leave it. I don't know if I can do daily.
[SEG0062] person_4 (DOCTOR): Try. Do not start the tranexamic again on your own.
[SEG0063] person_4 (DOCTOR): See me again in one week with the reports.
[SEG0064] person_2 (PATIENT): If I become worse in between? I don't know what is dangerous.
[SEG0065] person_4 (DOCTOR): If you are dizzy to the point of nearly fainting, or a pad soaks fully within one hour, come to emergency the same day. Otherwise the one week visit is enough.
[SEG0066] person_1 (NURSE): Shall I walk her to blood collection, doctor? They can draw it now.
[SEG0067] person_4 (DOCTOR): Yes. Full blood count, ferritin, TSH. I have ticked the form.
[SEG0068] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): We will be back in a week. Her son has a test at school tomorrow, that is the only rush.
[SEG0069] person_2 (PATIENT): Thank you, doctor. I will try the iron daily. I hope the tests are okay.

spec.situation: Tired, breathless woman with heavy periods for a year; counts pads and clots in vague terms; takes iron 'sometimes'; hair loss; relative mentions thyroid in the family. Blood tests, maybe pelvic scan.
features: doctor_thinks_aloud: the doctor lists possible causes or says what they will not conclude yet. Only record a clinical assessment if the doctor actually states a leading or differential impression; 'let's see what the tests say' is not an assessment.
self_correction: a speaker states a number, drug name or duration and then corrects it in the same turn or later ('seventy-five... no, hundred and fifty'). The label holds only the corrected value.
ambiguous_answer: an answer that sounds like yes but is really 'maybe' ('mm, I suppose', 'sometimes, not really'); recorded with uncertainty or not at all, never as a firm fact.

stopped_or_never_taken: a medicine the patient stopped, was never given or only took once ('I stopped it in March'). Status discontinued, not current; a medicine never taken is not recorded as a medication.

bad.reason: Tiredness and onset supported; duration uncertain: patient says six months, then one year.
bad.text: tiredness (category=constitutional, status=present, duration=1 year, onset=came along with the heavy periods, temporality=current, reported_by=patient, certainty=certain)

omissions.text: Heavy menstrual bleeding soaks through at night, with sheets stained, and she changes pads three to four times overnight.
Chest pain was asked about and not clearly affirmed or denied; patient said 'sometimes. Not really. I don't know.'
Possible unintentional weight loss was discussed: patient was unsure, said clothes may be loose, and had not checked on a scale.
Patient had never previously had a TSH test.
Folic acid had been prescribed previously on the same slip but the patient never took it, not even once.
Tranexamic acid was stopped last year after two days because it caused acidity.
Pelvic ultrasound is not being arranged now.
Blood tests were to be done today/now, with blood collection immediately after the visit.
